surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $1.94, well above the $1.56 consensus and also above the preview’s estimated $1.70–$1.75 buy-side whisper. It even exceeded the preview’s $1.78–$1.88 bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $1.94, up $0.40 (26%) year-over-year and well ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 Consensus” non-GAAP EPS: “$1.56”; preview estimate for the “real buy-side whisper”: “$1.70–1.75”; bull scenario: “$1.78–1.88.”

surprises.description: Bookings were $482 million, far below the preview’s greater-than-$600 million bogey and within its bear-case range of less than $500 million. This missed the preview’s key test for a return to above-parity bookings.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bookings / book-to-bill bogey: “>$600M / >1.0x”; the bear case called for “bookings <$500M.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue guidance of $621–$636 million implies a midpoint below both the preview’s roughly $645 million implied Q4 revenue and its $630 million base-case floor. The range also falls short of the preview’s $640 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue guidance of $621-$636 million implies 10% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calculated “~$645M” implied Q4 revenue, gave a base-case Q4 guide of “$630–655M,” and flagged “≥$640M” as a bull-case signal.

surprises.description: Full-year EPS guidance rose to $6.72–$6.82, above the prior $6.30–$6.50 range cited in the preview. The increase is a stronger upgrade than the preview’s base case of guidance narrowed to the upper half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year EPS outlook to $6.72-$6.82.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (raised July 28): … non-GAAP EPS $6.30–6.50”; the base case expected FY26 guidance to be “narrowed to upper half.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $2.37–$2.385 billion, putting the midpoint near the low end of the prior $2.37–$2.41 billion range rather than in the upper half anticipated in the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company … narrowed full-year revenue guidance to $2.37-$2.385 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior FY2026 revenue range was “$2.37–2.41B”; the base case expected guidance “narrowed to upper half.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 41.3%, above the preview’s roughly 40–41% estimate and its 40.5% threshold for evidence of structural margin strength. That is notable given the preview’s concern that returning Networked volume could dilute margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 350 basis points year-over-year to 41.3%, driven by favorable mix, operational efficiencies and cost discipline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adj. gross margin estimate: “~40–41%”; the preview said “≥40.5% = structural” and asked whether mix would dilute as Networked ramps.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $115 million, around $10 million above the preview’s estimate of approximately $105 million. Non-GAAP operating income also grew 20% on only 3% revenue growth, showing more earnings leverage than the preview’s estimates implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA set a new quarterly record at $115 million (19% of revenue), and non-GAAP operating income grew 20% on just 3% revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adj. EBITDA estimate: “~$105M (est.)”; the preview described a margin-driven EPS beat as the base case but did not anticipate this EBITDA level.

surprises.description: Backlog ended the quarter at $4.3 billion, below the preview’s $4.4 billion minimum bogey and down from the $4.4 billion reported for Q2. This did not deliver the hoped-for stabilization or increase in the demand signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total backlog of $4.3 billion at quarter end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Backlog bogey: “≥$4.4B, ideally up”; the preview cited Q2 backlog of “$4.4B flat q/q.”

surprises.description: ARR reached approximately $423 million, below the preview’s greater-than-$430 million bogey. However, its year-over-year growth accelerated to about 25% from 21% last quarter, partially offsetting the shortfall against the stated target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual recurring revenue grew approximately 25% year-over-year to $423 million, accelerating from 21% growth last quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: ARR / licensed apps bogey: “ARR >$430M”; the preview cited prior-quarter ARR of “$417M (+21%).”

surprises.description: Management identified a large gas distribution opportunity that has not yet entered bookings, with awards expected over the next two to three years. The preview did not flag this specific longer-term source of potential demand, though the extended award timeline means it is not a near-term bookings benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A large gas distribution opportunity remains ahead of bookings with awards expected over the next 2-3 years.”
